messages.author: 940e5abdb141a254
messages.subject: Dynamic Topic Model
parts:
Hi,

I'm new to Stan, so I'm hoping someone can point me in the right direction regarding my implementation of Dynamic Topic Models (Blei and Lafferty 2006). The code compiles, but when it runs, I get the following error.

Error in function stan::prob::normal_log(m): Random variable (max size) is 2, but must be consistent, 1 or max=10Rejecting proposed initial value with zero density.
Initialization failed after 100 attempts.  Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values, or reparameterizing the model.
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

Below is my model.

Thanks,
Manish

data {
    int<lower=2> K; //num topics
    int<lower=2> V; // num terms
    int<lower=1> M; // num docs
    int<lower=1> N; // num word instances
    int<lower=1> T; // num time intervals
    int<lower=1,upper=V> w[N]; // word list from data
    int<lower=1,upper=M> word_doc[N]; // doc assignments for wordlist
    int<lower=1,upper=T> word_time[N]; // time assignments for wordlist
    int<lower=1,upper=T> doc_time[M]; // time assignments for wordlist
   
    //mean and variance for normal parameters
    vector[M] alpha_mu;
    vector[M] alpha_tau;
    vector[V] beta_mu;
    vector[V] beta_tau;
    vector[K] eta_tau;
}

parameters {
    vector[M] Alpha[T];  //topic distribs
    vector[V] Beta[T,K]; //word distribs
    vector[K] Eta[M];
}

transformed parameters {
    simplex[K] theta[M];
    simplex[V] beta_trans[T,K];
    for (m in 1:M)
        theta[m] <- softmax(Eta[m]);
    for (t in 1:T) {
        for (k in 1:K) {
            beta_trans[t,k] <- softmax(Beta[t,k]);
        }
    }
}
model {
    for (t in 1:T) {
        if (t==1) {
            Alpha[t] ~ normal(alpha_mu,alpha_tau);
        } else {
            Alpha[t] ~ normal(Alpha[t-1], alpha_tau);
        }
        for (k in 1:K) {
            if (t==1) {
                Beta[t,k] ~ normal(beta_mu,beta_tau);
            } else {
                Beta[t,k] ~ normal(Beta[t-1,k],beta_tau);
            }
        }
    }
    for (m in 1:M) {
        Eta[m] ~ normal(Alpha[doc_time[m]],eta_tau);
    }
    for (n in 1:N) {
        real gamma[K];
        for (k in 1:K)
            gamma[k] <- log(theta[word_doc[n],k]) + log(beta_trans[word_time[n],k,w[n]]);
        increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(gamma));
    }
}

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Dynamic Topic Model
parts:
Hi Manish,

This response is to answer your question. (I'm not familiar enough with this model to know whether it makes sense to implement it in Stan.)

I believe the error is in this line:

Eta[m] is a K-vector.
Alpha[doc_time[m]] is a M-vector.

This doesn't work in Stan because it's expecting both vectors to be the same size.



Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Dynamic Topic Model
parts:
If you get this working and want to send it to us,
I can include it (with attribution, of course), in the
LDA section of the manual.

You might want to look at all the warnings in the manual
about trying to do Bayesian inference with topic models
(or other mixture models) --- there's a chapter on problematic
posteriors.

One thing that would be nice to explore is whether having
K parameters and applying softmax is effective for sampling,
or whether it's better to have (K-1) parameters and fix one
to 0, then do softmax. The (K-1) version is better identified
in the classical sense, but the K version is more symmetric
in terms of applying priors.

- Bob

P.S. We're working with Dave Blei (and his crew of students
and postdocs) on implementing black-box VB inference in Stan.
That'll give us pretty good implementations of all the LDA
models.
